note: ONE shared expectation for two resolvers that cannot call each other. The macOS shell (Sources/HasnaConversationsCore) decides which store the bundled server will use and then builds the environment it hands that server; src/lib/store/index.ts is what the server actually resolves with. They diverged: the shell read 3 env vars, the resolver honours more, and uncovered ones select the local store — so the shell logged store=hosted while the child served local SQLite, silently. Client transport is the API url + key pair alone (owner directive 2026-07-29; knowledge k_ms5wv466_u0jidq). Each arm below carries the input, what the shell must announce, and the exact store-selecting keys the child must receive. Tests/HasnaConversationsCoreTests asserts the shell half; src/lib/store/store-resolution-matrix.test.ts asserts the TypeScript resolver reaches the same store from that child environment. Neither half can drift without the other's test failing.

arms.name: arm1-prefixed-url-and-key
arms.note: The fleet flip signal. Correct before and after the fix.

arms.name: arm2-inherited-prefixed-db-path-outranks-url-and-key
arms.note: The DB path is the resolver's highest-precedence signal among valid selectors — the shell announces local and the child gets local. The child env carries the DB path and nothing else.

arms.name: arm3-inherited-unprefixed-db-path-outranks-url-and-key
arms.note: Same as arm2 through the unprefixed alias, which the old shell could not see at all.

arms.name: arm6-unprefixed-url-and-key-only
arms.note: The mirror-image failure: the old shell saw neither key and refused to start on a configuration the resolver accepts. Failing closed, so an availability bug rather than a correctness one — now resolved and re-emitted under the canonical names.

arms.name: arm2f-fleet-config-beats-inherited-prefixed-db-path
arms.note: THE DEPLOYED SHAPE, and the one the owner is waiting on. The fleet config file names the hosted service; a stray inherited DB_PATH must not silently redirect the app to a different dataset. The file outranks the inherited environment and the DB_PATH never reaches the child.

arms.name: file-fleet-config-names-cloud
arms.note: The fleet config file alone, with nothing inherited, resolves to the hosted service.

arms.name: file-db-path-names-local

arms.name: env-db-path-only-names-local

arms.name: env-unprefixed-db-path-only-names-local

arms.name: file-pair-beats-inherited-key-only
arms.note: The file outranks the inherited environment: a stray inherited key cannot turn the file's cloud config into a refusal.

arms.name: file-pair-beats-inherited-url-only
arms.note: The file outranks the inherited environment: a stray inherited URL cannot turn the file's cloud config into a refusal.

arms.name: key-without-url-refuses

arms.name: non-http-url-refuses
arms.note: assertUsableApiUrl refuses a URL the transport could not use. Mirrored here so the shell does not start a server that will throw.

arms.name: nothing-configured-fails-closed
arms.note: The one deliberate divergence from the TypeScript resolver, and the reason this app exists: with nothing configured the library documents local SQLite as the single-operator default, while the app refuses to start. No child is launched, so the two cannot disagree about a running server.
